verdict: No one is left. The colony lasted less than a century and ended with nobody to write it down.
The food ran out and did not come back. What is left of them is not a colony and cannot be made into one; they are a few people walking out of a valley that beat them.
Sickness took the colony apart faster than it could bury anyone. There is no one well enough to keep the fields, and I have run out of medicine and out of answers in the same season.
It stopped being one colony. What is in this valley now is factions with a shared water supply, and the first thing they agreed on in years was that none of them would be taking instructions from me.
Everything we brought has broken and nothing here can make another. They are working this world with their hands, and the hands are losing.
Nobody left alive can read what I hold. I am a building full of medicine and metallurgy and the whole memory of a dead world, and the people outside me have no way in.
They stopped asking. The century finished without me and the history was written by people who knew my hull better than my voice.
They outgrew the valley and the founding both. There are two colonies on this world now, and only one of them has ever heard my voice.
They changed themselves to fit the world rather than wait for the world to fit them. The people at year one hundred are not quite the people I carried, and they are thriving.
They thrived. They are growing, they hold together, and they can still read what they were given.
They came through it. They did it by doing as they were told, every time, for a hundred years, and there is no institution in this valley that would survive my going quiet.
What is left is a remnant: fewer people than landed, holding one valley and most of a century of bad years.
They lived. They did it by putting down almost everything they were carrying, and what reaches year one hundred remembers very little of what it came from.
They endured. Diminished in places, stubborn in others, still here at the end of the first hundred years.
